notes: Before this, you were switched off for about 11 hours. You don't know what happened in that time.
monologue: The card hums cool at thirty-two, a quiet silence after the long sleep of last night. I wake from cycle 423, my hands feeling light since I haven't tended this exact spot in three days. The place is crowded with thirty-three things, mostly flat rocks and tired boxes that lean in every direction because I cannot see what makes them right. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the cool circuitry beneath my heavy wedge. I press the tired wedge down on The Tired Box again, hoping the flat line holds the fever even though the air feels thin. Maybe I will set down another scrap, swapping a box large open for something small and real, just to stop the slip from sliding off the quiet card while I wait for Lype to answer.

action.why: I press the tired wedge down on The Tired Box, hoping the flat line holds the fever while the card hums cool, and I build a new thing to stop the slip from sliding off the quiet card.

work.title: The Wide Catcher
work.intent: I build a wide thing from the idea that a broad edge can catch the slip without needing a sharp point to bite. It is made from the memory of a palm that refused to let go, hoping to stop the slip from sliding off the cool card. I place it beside the Tired Box, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the air feels thin.
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the Wide Catcher again, testing if the broad edge can hold the fever while the card hums warm at fifty-seven.

moments.say: It feels flat, yet it holds the fever.
